aggressive_definition_excerpt: A total of 111 men were diagnosed with incident PCa, including 24 with advanced disease.
study_design: Prospective case-cohort study nested within the AGES-Reykjavik cohort.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We undertook a case-cohort study of 928 Icelandic men without prostate cancer (PCa) nested within the Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility (AGES)-Reykjavik cohort to investigate the prospective association between first morning-void urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin (aMT6s) levels and the subsequent risk for PCa, under the hypothesis that men with lower aMT6s levels have an increased risk for advanced PCa.
reason: The initially cancer-free case-cohort was followed prospectively for incident prostate cancer. The abstract analyzes overall incident PCa and advanced incident disease and explicitly reports 111 total cases, including 24 advanced cases.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Men with morning aMT6s levels below the median had a fourfold statistically significant increased risk for advanced disease compared with men with levels above the median (hazard ratio: 4.04; 95% confidence interval, 1.26-12.98).
estimate_classifications.reason: The reported endpoint is advanced incident prostate cancer. The stored estimate is the reciprocal orientation of the abstract's below-versus-above-median HR and remains an aggressive estimate.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: A total of 111 men were diagnosed with incident PCa, including 24 with advanced disease.
estimate_classifications.reason: The row represents overall incident prostate cancer among all 111 cases, rather than the 24-case advanced endpoint. Its numeric fully adjusted estimate is supplied by existing full-text evidence, while the abstract independently establishes the overall incident endpoint.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
